## Summary

**Data source overview.** This AI Impacts page is an index/outline of the site's body of work on AI timeline predictions: the prediction sources themselves (expert surveys such as the 2016 Expert Survey on Progress in AI, Müller & Bostrom, Hanson, Kruel, FHI, AGI‑09, Bainbridge, Michie; the MIRI dataset of public statements; and written analyses such as Kurzweil's and Allen's), plus meta-level findings about how to interpret them (similarity of historical and contemporary predictions, falsification of the Maes‑Garreau law, publication bias toward short timelines, survey-vs-statement differences, optimism selection bias, group differences). The implicit safety-relevant reasoning chain runs from "AI safety planning depends on calibrated timelines" through specific bias mechanisms to concrete forecasting-methodology interventions.

**EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[76]** — The source is a link-outline, so most nodes are one-line summaries of *other* pages; details (sample sizes, statistics) are not present, forcing conservative confidence values and some moderate inference to build risk → problem → insight → rationale → mechanism → evidence → intervention chains. Instruction improvements that would help: (a) explicit guidance for *index/meta pages* whose content is a table of contents (e.g., whether to instantiate one node per linked study or to aggregate by method family); (b) guidance on whether *forecasting/epistemics* sources should be anchored to an inferred top-level AI risk (I did so, since no risk is stated explicitly); (c) a rule for how to represent "claim X is false" findings (I used validation-evidence nodes whose description states the refutation); (d) clarification on lifecycle coding for non-model-lifecycle governance/forecasting interventions (I used 6 = Other throughout).

**Inference strategy.** The page states no risk and no interventions. I applied moderate inference to (1) posit the top-level risk that miscalibrated human-level-AI timelines degrade AI safety planning (the stated purpose of AI Impacts' timeline work), and (2) convert methodological practices (surveys with concrete tasks, prediction datasets, bias testing, bias correction, metasurveys, critical review of analyses) into intervention nodes. All inferred edges carry confidence 1–2 and are flagged in their rationales; edges tied to explicitly stated findings (Maes‑Garreau falsification, survey-vs-statement gap, historical-similarity finding, Bainbridge/Michie results) carry confidence 3.

**Extraction completeness.** All six bias/accuracy considerations, all three evidence families (surveys, public statements, written analyses), the hardware-vs-software analytic dispute, and the blog-level themes (inside view, metasurvey, concrete tasks, why AGI researchers expect AI soon) are represented in the fabric. Individual survey instances with distinctive elicitation formats are aggregated into one mechanism node to avoid 8 near-duplicate satellites, while surveys with reported results (Bainbridge, Michie, Müller & Bostrom, ESPAI) are kept as separate validation-evidence nodes for cross-source merging.

**Key limitations.** No quantitative results are given on this page, so validation-evidence descriptions are thin; the hardware/software analysis branch rests on two one-line summaries; the risk node is inferred rather than stated; several intervention maturity ratings are inferred from the existence of the linked studies rather than from stated validation.
